reviews.body:
### 🟡 Changes recommended The cron seed test lacks an exact-match future-start case, leaving the behavior that prevents skipping an occurrence at the start unprotected against regression.
1 open issue - [Test cron occurrence exactly at the future start boundary](https://github.com/OpenAEV-Platform/openaev/pull/9735#discussion_r4673657658) · New
What changed in this PR Fixes #9575 by making the shared cron recurrence handler honor future start dates, preventing recurring scenarios from running before their configured start. **Changes:** - Uses one nanosecond before a future start as the cron reference, preserving occurrences exactly at the start. - Preserves next-occurrence behavior for starts in the past. - Adds focused regression tests for future and past starts. The fix stays appropriately localized to the shared recurrence handler. | File | Description | | ---- | ----------- | | `openaev-api/​src/​test/​java/​io/​openaev/​service/​period/​CronServiceSeedTest.java` | Adds future-start and past-start regression tests. | | `openaev-api/​src/​main/​java/​io/​openaev/​service/​period/​CronService.java` | Uses the recurrence seed to bound the next cron occurrence. |
Review effort: Balanced

review_comments.body: suggestion (non-blocking): Exercise a future start that exactly matches the cron expression, following the behavior-coverage guidance in `.github/instructions/testing.instructions.md`. The midnight start would pass even without `minusNanos(1)`, so it does not protect against skipping an occurrence exactly at the start. Using `2022-04-30T10:43:56Z` keeps the existing expected result and tests that boundary.
